checks: The halfspaces v_i·x≥0 cover K since the normals sum to zero. They meet its interior on both sides: choose A points strictly on either side of −1 and add a point on the corresponding B facet, then halve. Thus the proper-cap hypotheses hold even in the stronger sense of a cut crossing the interior.
At α=Q−U₃=q₃≥0 only q₁−q₃ and q₂−q₃ can contribute to the positive-part sum. This remains valid at ties. The cap count is d+1 in dimension d, so the coefficient is 1/Γ and the right bound is Q/Γ−F.
Substituting Q≤Γ(a+b+k)/2 gives k≤a+b−2F and Q≤Γ(a+b−F). The bound k≥b−a gives F≤a. Also κ>0 for all d≥2 since (1+1/d)^d>2.

The intersection of the two strict A complements has volume at least a−U₁−U₂≥κU₃>0 by properness. At one common point its remaining margins sum strictly above 2 before adding the d−1 ones in the H_i. Multiplication by db/(d+1) gives the strict reserve. Summing the two dimension-three local inequalities preserves each radical, and the reserve supplies the strict 3b term.
Original b69ebda3a2e6d72a §5 (7)–(10) uses the same shared point, same Q assumptions and same normalization.

dependencies.hypotheses: The ordinary body K in dimension d is covered by d+1 proper closed halfspaces with cap masses q_i. The cutoff q₃ is nonnegative and the theorem's dimension/cap-count parameter is d.
